description: End states every sync engine must reach. One device and the cloud start in agreement on one note (`synced`). The device then acts offline (`local`) while another device changes the cloud (`elsewhere`), and the device syncs. `expected` lists the notes on the device and in the cloud afterwards, as "title: content", sorted. Engines that can download and upload separately (web, Rust) run every case in each of `orders` and must reach the same end state both ways: AUD-I01 was exactly an outcome that depended on the order. Kotlin syncs in one call and runs each case once. Nothing may be lost: a conflict ends with both versions somewhere.

cases.name: an offline edit with nothing changed elsewhere is uploaded
an edit made elsewhere is downloaded
two different edits keep both: the other device's on the note, ours as a copy
the same edit made on both devices is not duplicated
an offline edit of a note deleted elsewhere survives as a copy
a note deleted elsewhere and untouched here is deleted here
an offline delete with nothing changed elsewhere is deleted in the cloud
an offline delete loses to an edit made elsewhere: the note comes back with those words
a note deleted on both devices stays deleted
a note created offline is uploaded alongside the synced one
